title: A Tug-of-War Between Static and Dynamic Memory in Intel SGX
problem: Intel SGX enclaves balance static memory (allocated at enclave creation) and dynamic memory (allocated at runtime). Improper allocation strategy causes significant performance degradation due to expensive page management operations.
method: Profile-guided optimizer (Harmony) analyzing impact of dynamic memory management on application performance. Suggests near-optimal static/dynamic memory distribution based on profiling.

title: Self-Attention to Operator Learning-based 3D-IC Thermal Simulation
problem: Efficient thermal simulation for 3D ICs with high power densities; traditional PDE-solving methods are accurate but computationally slow for iterative design workflows.
method: Self-Attention UNet Fourier Neural Operator (SAU-FNO) combines self-attention mechanisms with U-Net architecture and FNO to capture long-range dependencies and model local high-frequency features effectively. Transfer learning fine-tunes low-fidelity training data to reduce dependence on extensive high-fidelity datasets and accelerate training.

title: Destination Earth: The Climate Change Adaptation Digital Twin
problem: Traditional climate modeling at high resolution (km-scale) is computationally infeasible; digital twin for climate adaptation requires multi-decadal simulations.
method: Multi-decadal global climate projections at 5 km resolution using three coupled Earth system models on LUMI and MareNostrum5; scaling to 1 km demonstrated.

title: Anda: Unlocking Efficient LLM Inference with a Variable-Length Grouped Activation Data Format
problem: Weight-only quantized LLMs retain floating-point (FP) activations for accuracy, which shifts the energy and latency bottleneck to costly FP memory accesses and FP-INT GEMM computation; existing LLM accelerators optimize computation alone without jointly addressing data representation and movement for FP activations.
method: Anda proposes a new adaptive activation data type with a group-shared exponent and dynamically allocated mantissa bits per group, enabling variable precision per LLM module. An iterative post-training precision search algorithm determines per-module bit-widths to balance accuracy and efficiency without retraining. On the hardware side, Anda uses a bit-plane-based data organization, bit-serial computation processing elements, and a runtime bit-plane compressor to simultaneously shrink storage, computation, and memory footprint. The result is a hardware-software co-designed accelerator targeting FP-INT GEMM in LLMs.

title: ChipletEM: Physics-Based 2.5D and 3D Chiplet Heterogeneous Integration Electromigration Signoff Tool Using Coupled Stress and Thermal Simulation
problem: Electromigration (EM) in 2.5D/3D chiplet heterogeneous integration systems is inadequately understood; existing EM research ignores Through Silicon Vias (TSVs) and non-uniform thermal distribution between dies, causing signoff errors and missing critical failure modes.
method: ChipletEM couples electrical-thermal simulation using finite volume method (FVM) for initial temperature and current density in TSVs, finite difference time domain (FDTD) solver for hydrostatic stress (nucleation and post-voiding), thermal migration effects, and analytical TSV thermal solver. Components are coupled at each timestep to simulate interactions between EM stress, thermal stress, void growth, resistance change, IR drop, and Joule heating.

title: Query-Based Black-Box Stealthy Sensor Attacks on Cyber-Physical Systems
problem: Designing stealthy sensor attacks on cyber-physical systems under black-box conditions (minimal knowledge of target system) requires maintaining attack stealthiness both in output (avoiding detector alerts) and during attack generation (limiting detector queries).
method: Query-based black-box attack framework using active learning to extract detector information into a time series model without triggering alerts. The framework maintains stealthiness during training via adaptive query budgeting and generates attack sequences from the learned model that bypass CPS safety constraints.

title: Implementing support for Interactive and AI workloads in a traditional HPC environment
problem: Interactive and AI workloads conflict with batch HPC jobs in traditional scheduling; incompatible QoS requirements
method: Slurm job scheduling technique: short runtimes for all jobs, resource-limited high-priority QOS

title: Virtuoso: Enabling Fast and Accurate Virtual Memory Research via an Imitation-based Operating System Simulation Methodology
problem: Existing virtual memory (VM) simulation tools either lack accuracy in modeling OS software components (e.g., page table walks, TLB shootdowns, OS scheduling interactions) or are too slow and complex to prototype hardware/OS co-designs spanning the hardware/software boundary.
method: Virtuoso introduces an imitation-based OS simulation methodology where a lightweight simulator imitates the behavior of a full OS by training on traces of OS decisions (page allocation, eviction, TLB management) captured from real OS runs, then replaying those decisions with hardware-accurate timing in a fast simulation framework. This enables rapid iteration over hardware/OS co-design points without full OS simulation overhead.

title: CORSAIR: An In-Memory Computing Chiplet Architecture for Inference-Time Compute Acceleration
problem: AI inference workloads suffer from high memory bandwidth requirements and latency during matrix operations; CORSAIR proposes a chiplet-based in-memory computing architecture to bring computation closer to data storage.
method: CORSAIR uses a modular chiplet architecture where each chiplet integrates analog or mixed-signal in-memory computing fabric with local memory, enabling matrix operations directly in the memory substrate while maintaining chiplet-level flexibility through standard interconnects.

title: State Machine Orchestration of an HPC Workflow in Cloud
problem: Porting HPC workflows between cloud and on-premises environments is non-trivial; existing designs may not efficiently leverage cloud-native orchestration frameworks.
method: Redesign MuMMI ensemble workflow for Kubernetes: progression from traditional HPC to fully portable cloud variant; compare service/filesystem-based vs event-driven orchestration.

title: PrOFraC: Property Ordering and Frame Clause Reuse for Multi-Property Verification
problem: Multi-property formal verification scales poorly; sequential property proving inefficient; design complexity rising
method: PrOFraC: initial design unfolding + goal restructuring + modified PDR starting from latest frame + statistical reordering

title: NearFetch: Saving Inter-Module Bandwidth in Many-Chip-Module GPUs
problem: In many-chip-module (MCM) GPUs, inter-module bandwidth is physically constrained by organic substrate or silicon interposer manufacturing limits, and fetching data from remote modules causes bandwidth contention that reduces effective achieved bandwidth, degrading GPU performance on high-sharing workloads.
method: NearFetch is a routing-based solution that exploits data locality across GPU modules on the routing path between a requesting module and remote memory. When a memory request traverses intermediate GPU modules, NearFetch checks if those intermediate modules already hold the requested data locally; if so, data is forwarded from the nearer intermediate module rather than from the distant memory partition. A topology-aware Miss Status Handling Register (MSHR) coalescing scheme records memory address information to support future forwarding decisions on cache misses. NearFetch introduces a new Inter-Module Bandwidth per Access (IBPA) metric to quantify bandwidth waste from multi-hop fetches.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Covert Channel and Side Channel Vulnerabilities Introduced by RowHammer Defenses
problem: Modern RowHammer defenses (PRAC, RFM) introduce timing covert and side channels because their preventive refresh actions block DRAM access in ways that depend on application memory access patterns, allowing adversaries to both observe victim access behavior and establish covert communication channels. No prior work has analyzed these defense-induced timing vulnerabilities.
method: The paper introduces LeakyHammer, a class of attacks exploiting the timing latency increase caused by RowHammer preventive refresh actions. Two covert channels are built: one exploiting PRAC's per-row activation counter responses and one exploiting RFM's refresh management commands, both causing measurable DRAM latency spikes observable by a spy process. A proof-of-concept website fingerprinting attack identifies visited websites by correlating RowHammer-preventive action patterns triggered by a victim's browsing. Three countermeasures (randomized refresh scheduling, access pattern obfuscation, and noise injection) are evaluated.

title: FIGLUT: An Energy-Efficient Accelerator Design for FP-INT GEMM Using Look-Up Tables
problem: Weight-only quantization for LLM deployment produces FP-INT mixed-precision GEMM operations where one operand is floating-point (activations) and the other is low-bit integer (weights); this FP-INT compute is difficult to implement efficiently on conventional GPU multiply-accumulate hardware.
method: FIGLUT implements GEMM using a look-up table (LUT) approach: rather than performing FP-INT multiplications directly, the hardware precomputes all possible products of the floating-point activation values with each possible weight pattern and stores them in LUTs. At inference time, the LUT is indexed by weight bits to retrieve the precomputed partial product. A half-size LUT variant is introduced along with a dedicated decoding and multiplexing unit to reduce LUT storage overhead. The design supports multiple bit precisions and quantization methods in a single fixed hardware configuration.

title: Klotski: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference via Expert-Aware Multi-Batch Pipeline
problem: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs with trillion-scale parameters must be offloaded to CPU/disk memory when GPU VRAM is insufficient, but each expert's compute time per token is shorter than the I/O time to load it, creating large pipeline bubbles that negate the benefit of overlapping I/O and computation.
method: Klotski introduces an expert-aware multi-batch pipeline that maintains multiple batches in flight simultaneously and schedules which experts to prefetch and compute based on expert routing decisions across batches. By batching tokens that activate the same expert across multiple concurrent requests, Klotski increases per-expert compute volume to exceed I/O time, eliminating pipeline bubbles. The system tracks expert access patterns across batches and uses an expert prefetching scheduler that co-optimizes I/O and compute assignment to saturate both the memory bus and compute units.

title: CND-IDS: Continual Novelty Detection for Intrusion Detection Systems
problem: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems struggle with two critical challenges: streaming network traffic that changes over time, and the lack of labels for novel (zero-day) attacks.
method: CND-IDS combines a continually-updated learning-based feature extractor that adapts feature representations to new system data with a novelty detector using PCA reconstruction to identify anomalies, eliminating dependence on attack labels.
